title: Where the Foot Is: A Leg of Three Joints, Its Forward and Inverse Kinematics, the Two Knees, and the Straight Leg

questions.question: How many answers has the inverse kinematics of a leg for a place within reach?
options: Two, with the knee bent one way or the other
One: three joints and three coordinates leave no choice
Four: two for the knee and two for the lean
As many as there are leans, since the offset can turn either way
questions.explanation: The lean is fixed by the foot's place across the body, and the thigh and shank are then a two link problem with the knee angle plus or minus an arccosine. A robot picks one sign and keeps it.

questions.question: Over a grid of 756 places, how many were reachable?
options: 756, every place on the grid
378, half, since only one knee direction counts
76, the ones directly under the hip
questions.explanation: The 76 refused were nearer the lean axis than the hip's offset or further away than the leg is long. Each of the 680 came back to the place asked.

questions.question: A place 0.50 m below the hip:
options: Was reached with the knee straight
Was reached by leaning the leg sideways
Was reached, but only with the knee bent forward
Was out of reach
questions.explanation: The thigh and shank are 0.21 m each, so the foot can be at most 0.42 m from the hip's pitch axis. The function says false and makes nothing up.

questions.question: The knee was -89 degrees for the foot 0.30 m below the hip, which is:
options: Nearly straight, as at full stretch
Bent forward, as a person's knee
Folded as far as it goes
Bent back, as a standing dog's
questions.explanation: With two links of 0.21 m and the foot 0.30 m below, the knee is close to a right angle, bent back. A lower stand bends it more.

questions.question: Why is the straight leg a singularity?
options: The foot cannot move farther along the leg and the joint rates grow without bound near it
The motors have no torque left when the leg is straight
The inverse kinematics has no answer for a straight leg
The two knee answers are furthest apart there
questions.explanation: At full stretch the two knee answers become one, and no joint motion moves the foot further out. Near it a small foot movement along the leg needs a very large joint rate.

questions.question: What is not in this model?
options: The sideways offset of the hip's pitch axis
Joint limits, backlash and the true zeros of the joints
The difference between a left leg and a right one
The places the leg cannot reach
questions.explanation: The model is the ideal geometry. A real leg has angles it cannot reach, play in its gears, and zeros that are not where the model says, which 34-08 measures.
